properties.Overview: The development of an unnamed hyperscale data center has been proposed just 10 miles North of Northern Cheyenne jurisdiction, near Colstrip, MT. In addition to the data center, a small nuclear modular reactor (SMR) has also been proposed to help power the data center. There is also the potential development of a uranium enrichment facility and nuclear waste storage facility to support the SMR’s existence. Both of which will have detrimental impacts on Northern Cheyenne homelands’ land, air, and People

Quantica Infrastructure, a new company that provides land and power for data centers, is planning to build a 5,000-acre energy and digital infrastructure campus near Billings, Montana. Dubbed the "Big Sky Campus," the project will initially offer 500 MW of renewable power and battery storage, with the potential to expand to 1 GW. Construction is set to begin in 2026. NorthWestern Energy Group will provide energy services for the campus. The initial electric service for the first phase is expected to begin as early as 2026, with the load reaching 500 MW by 2030.
Planned expansion as part of Quantica Big Sky Campus.

Atlanta-based TAC Data Centers is set to invest between $1 billion and $1.5 billion in a new 569-acre development in Montana, adjacent to the AgriTech Park. This ambitious project, dubbed Project Cardinal, will encompass 2 million square feet (185,805 sqm) of data center space. Construction is slated to kick off in 2026. The first buildings, ranging from 135,000 to 200,000 square feet (12,540-18,580 sqm), are expected to be operational by late 2027 or early 2028. The company anticipates the entire campus will be fully built out by 2030. TAC Data Centers is a wholly-owned data center platform of The Ardent Companies. It's important to note that this is a distinct entity from Northern Data's Ardent Data Centers unit.
Planned expansion as part of TAC Great Falls Campus.
Binary Net acquired the data center in May 2019 when the company acquired Lincoln Data Investments (LDI) as a subsidiary. It is now known as Lincoln Data Centers.

properties.Overview: Google's newest data center, roughly 580 acres in Nebraska.

AAIM's Nebraska 1 data center, operational since October 2024, achieved an impressive feat by launching just five months after its May 2024 groundbreaking. A key highlight of this facility is the incorporation of Nebraska's first privately held substation, running at 67kV.

The Adams County Planning and Zoning Commission has recommended approving a permit for the county's first commercial cryptocurrency mining data center. This facility would be built on 2.64 acres, roughly half a mile west of the CPI Hayland elevator near Prosser. To power the operation, AAIM plans to construct a 12.5-megawatt substation, connecting to Southern Power District's electrical supply.
This data center is a part of Google's Omaha Campus.

A 340-acre data center project known as Project Anthem at the intersection of 11th Street and the west side of the Creek Turnpike is being proposed in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Construction on the $800 million site is set to take three years. It's unclear which company is behind Project Anthem. Tulsa World suggests it could be Meta, based on the investment amount matching other projects from the social media firm. Neither Tulsa, nor Oklahoma more generally, has a major data center ecosystem.

An undisclosed company has submitted a rezoning application for 506 acres in Tulsa County, proposing to change the land's classification from agricultural (AG) to industrial. This land, currently owned by Bird Creek Ranch Limited Partnership, is located north and west of the intersection of E 76th Street N and North Sheridan Road. The company plans to develop a data center campus, code-named Project Clydesdale, on the site.

Stillwater's Planning Commission has unanimously approved the first two phases, each comprising approximately 300,000 square feet. Phase I could be operational by 2027. Each data center is projected to generate tax revenue equivalent to 250 new houses valued at $300,000 each, bringing significant economic benefits to the city, state, and country.

properties.Project_Name: Vantage: Port Washington Campus, Wisconsin North Phase
properties.Overview: Aquired from Cloverleaf Infrastructure partners in 2025, Vantage Data Centers plans to build a data center complex in Port Washington on up to 1,900 acres, potentially making it one of the world's largest. While Vantage hasn't officially announced its plans, discussions between Cloverleaf and city officials indicate the campus could span 1,900 acres and consume 3.5 gigawatts of electricity. Conceptual plans for the campus include 11 data center buildings and five substations. These buildings will house thousands of interconnected computers, using fiber optic cables to connect to the outside world. This infrastructure is essential for powering a vast array of modern online services, including social media, video streaming, cloud storage, banking, air traffic control, and increasingly, AI tools. The development is expected to unfold in two to three phases. Construction on the initial phase could begin in Fall 2025 and be completed by 2027. The entire complex is projected to take 6 to 10 years to build out, with full completion anticipated between 2030 and 2035.

A company called Balloonist LLC proposed a $1.6 Billion data center project to Menomonie City Council in 2024. The council approved annexing and rezoning about 320 acres of farmland for the project. Balloonist LLC has not disclosed who will operate the completed project.

properties.Overview: Crusoe has partnered with Tallgrass to develop a gigawatt-scale AI data center campus in Wyoming. Located just south of Cheyenne near the Colorado state line, the project is designed to expand up to 10GW. It will utilize a mix of natural gas and future renewable energy sources, benefiting from Tallgrass' nearby CO2 sequestration hub for carbon capture and its existing natural gas and water infrastructure in the state.
Related Digital is aiming to develop a 115-acre campus in Wyoming.

Construction of the Wyoming Hyperscale White Box data center began in 2022 on a 58-acre plot near Aspen Mountain in Evanston, Wyoming. This project aims to set a new standard for environmentally-friendly, highly efficient data centers that also contribute positively to local communities. The data center is being built on land owned by Thornock's family, which has been involved in ranching for 6 generations. The location benefits from ready access to renewable energy from nearby wind and solar farms. The initial phase of the Evanston project is scheduled to become operational in the first quarter of 2026, marking the debut of its first facilities. Wyoming Hyperscale has merged with Prometheus Hyperscale, expanding their initial project into plans for a massive 1 GW data center campus.

In 2022, Meta announced plans for a mega expansion of the Eagle Mountain Site. This latest addition, consisting of two buildings, will increase the campus by approximately 2 million square feet. The expansion will bring Meta's total capital investment in the Eagle Mountain project to $1.5 billion.

In 2022, Meta announced plans for a mega expansion of the Eagle Mountain Site. This latest addition, consisting of two buildings, will increase the campus by approximately 2 million square feet. The expansion will bring Meta's total capital investment in the Eagle Mountain project to $1.5 billion.

Meta is developing a 715,000 sq ft (66,425 sqm) data center campus in Cheyenne, Wyoming. The company plans to invest over $800 million in the 960-acre project, which it says will be optimized for AI workloads. The campus will include at least two buildings and on-site substations. Notably, these buildings will not follow Meta's traditional H design used in previous projects. Construction on the first building started in early 2024 and the facility is scheduled to open by 2027. Wyoming offers tax breaks for data center operators, which is said to have been a deciding factor in Meta pursuing the Cheyenne project. A data center development on the site, dubbed ‘Project Cosmo’, was approved by Cheyenne City Council in November 2023. At the time, Meta was using the shell company Goat Systems LLC to conduct business. The social media firm was named as the company behind the project in May 2024.

Facebook, is looking to expand its data center campus outside Richmond, Virginia. The company has acquired a large portion of land close to its existing data center within Henrico County’s White Oak Technology Park and is looking to develop more data centers under the name ‘Project Tropical’. The 475-acre plot was sold by the County’s Economic Development Authority for $35.2 million at the end of October 2022. The company has since filed to develop two data centers at 3951 Portugee Road, next to a substation and south across the road from its existing Henrico campus.

Meta, previously known as Facebook, has begun construction on a new data center in Kuna, Idaho. This 960,000-square-foot facility represents an $800 million investment by the social media giant. Once completed, it will be Meta's 15th data center in the United States and its 19th worldwide. The project, which was initially developed under the codename "Project Peregrine," broke ground in September 2022. Construction is expected to last until 2025, marking a significant expansion of Meta's data infrastructure.
This data center is a part of Meta's Kuna Campus in Idaho.

Applied Digital's data center in Ellendale is located in Dickey County, North Dakota. It was initially designed for cryptocurrency mining operations. However, it is now being developed into an HPC facility as Applied Digital pivots to offer more AI-related services. This Facility will be part of Applied Digital's Ellendale campus.

Aurum Capital Ventures, Inc. is looking to acquire land in Bismarck for a new data center. They are considering 300 acres of county-owned land in east Bismarck, located at the same address as the Buckstop Junction historical village. Additionally, Aurum is interested in purchasing several hundred acres of state-owned land situated just north of the county property.

properties.Project_Name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2 project, ND
properties.Overview: AI data center firm Applied Digital, formerly a cryptomine company, has announced a new $3 billion data center campus called Polaris Forge 2 near Fargo, North Dakota. The 900-acre campus, located in Harwood, Cass County, will use Applied Digital's liquid-cooled design. Groundbreaking is scheduled for September 2025, with initial capacity expected in 2026. The two-building campus is projected to reach full capacity by early 2027. The project has already secured power from Cass County Electric Cooperative.

Enerfore Digital is building a data center in Dry Fork Township, Williams County, North Dakota. The facility will occupy 20,000 square feet (2,000 square meters) on a 10-acre site, dedicated to cryptomining operations. In October 2024, the company received approval to apply for a conditional use permit for the project. No date has been scheduled for the Williams County Planning and Zoning Commission to approve the proposal, but Enerfore is aiming for its data center to be operational in early 2025.

properties.Project_Name: Teton Digital: Project Trinity Dry Fork Township, ND
properties.Overview: Wyoming-based Teton Digital has received approval to develop a data center in North Dakota. Known as Project Trinity, the facility will be situated eight miles south of Tioga on a 25-acre portion of an 80-acre site in Dry Fork Township. The development will occur in two phases, with the first phase scheduled to become operational by the third or fourth quarter of 2025, utilizing existing power from a nearby substation. The second phase involves the construction of a 100MW+ substation in collaboration with local utility MWEC and the full completion of the data center by the end of 2026.

properties.Project_Name: Critical data house: Project Fighting Pike, Williston, ND
properties.Overview: Under the codename Project Fighting Pike, Critical Data House (CDH) is developing a new 300-acre campus in Williams County. The development includes seven buildings, ranging from 275,000 to 500,000 sq ft (25,550 to 46,450 sqm). These facilities will utilize a closed-loop cooling system with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Data center master plan submitted to City of Williston was approved on March 17 th , 2025. Construction is slated for Q2 2025 to Q4 2027, with the first phase involving two buildings. The full three-phase build-out is anticipated to take ten years, representing a potential investment of $5 billion by CDH, with an additional $5 billion for IT hardware. Two (2) pre-cast concrete partners standing by to begin work casting concrete tilt up walls. 300 laborers dedicated to this scope of work. Three (3) fiber carriers available to provide dark and lit fiber to Denver, Chicago, MSP, Lincoln and Omaha and Seattle. Pioneer power generation plant-600 megawatts-operating today. 300-megawatt power will serve letter in hand with an option to grow to 600 megawatts.

Atlas Power is developing a $1.9 billion cryptocurrency mining facility in Williston, North Dakota. The project was announced in January 2022, with plans for a 700 MW capacity to be built in three phases. The Atlas facility currently consumes about 240 megawatts.

Applied Digital is proposing a "multi-billion-dollar" AI data center development in South Dakota, east of Toronto. This ambitious project could attract up to $16 billion in investment and is expected to generate 200 high-paying jobs. The initial phase of the development involves constructing two buildings, each spanning 907,000 square feet (84,263 square meters). The project timeline estimates six to nine months for zoning and state-level approvals, followed by an 18 to 24-month construction period.
Currently South Dakota's largest proposed data center

Property development firm Oppidan and Rockport LLC is proposing to build a technology park in Apple Valley in Dakota County, Minnesota. They would like to develop 7 buildings, on 1 million sq ft (92,900 sqm). 5 of the buildings are planned to be data centers.
properties.Status: Planned - Propsed (Multi-phase for total of 5 buildings)

properties.Overview: Amazon has suspended plans for this data center in Becker, Minnesota. Site history: Amazon Data Services acquired 348 acres in Becker, Minnesota for $73.6 million to develop a data center project. The land was previously part of Xcel Energy Inc.'s Sherco Site. Amazon is proposing to install 250 diesel generators at its planned data center. The transaction involved several ownership changes: Elk River Technologies first purchased the parcel from Xcel Energy in April 2024 for $7.97 million, then sold it to Amazon—representing a substantial price increase in a short period. This development comes after earlier plans for the site fell through in 2022, when negotiations between Xcel Energy and Google for a potential data center project were unsuccessful. In February 2024, Microsoft bought 300 acres of land from Xcel nearby in Becker.

Microsoft has purchased land from Xcel Energy in Becker for a future data center. The tech giant bought about 295 acres in the city of Becker for about $17.7 million, according to public data from the Minnesota Department of Revenue.
Operated by AAIM, this data center is a 7.5MW site in Minnesota.
Tract is planning to build a massive data center campus, with two data centers in Randolph Township, Minnesota.

The company plans to invest a total of $1 billion in the new Chaska center for a total of 1.4 million sqft. The building will have a footprint of 713,000 square feet and, at its highest point, be 72 feet tall. A 30-foot-tall berm will wrap around the northern and eastern side of the site, helping separate the building from residential areas.

CLOP Eagan MN, LLC, with involvement from Oppidan, is developing a 61,000 square foot data center on a 22.1-acre portion of YMCA-owned land on Opperman Drive in Eagan, Minnesota. The project, on land subdivided in the early 1990s, has begun construction in June 2025, with full operation expected by December 2026. Oppidan lists Connect Data Centers as a subsidiary

Archer Datacenters has expanded its footprint in Minnesota, securing an expansive 87.6-acre property in Faribault for $4.5 million. The land, purchased from local firm PK LaRoche LLP, is set to become a significant data center development site. The company's conceptual plan involves constructing up to six buildings, with each facility ranging from 44,000 to 107,000 square feet. When fully developed, the site will offer approximately 500,000 square feet of single-story data center capacity, powered by an on-site electrical substation.

Tract is pursuing plans for a $5 billion data center development at the Farmington Technology Park in Dakota County, Minnesota. The proposal encompasses 343 acres, including the Fountain Valley Golf Club property. Despite objections from some residents, the Farmington City Council voted to approve the final plat and planned unit development on November 18, 2024. The proposed site plan envisions up to 12 data center buildings spanning more than 2.5 million square feet, along with two administrative buildings.
Oppidan plans to build a large technology park on approximately 140 acres in Hampton, Minnesota. Oppidan lists Connect Data Centers as a subsidiary focused on data center development.

The "Alternative Urban Area Review" document was unanimously approved by Hermantown's City council on Oct 6th 2025. the facility will consist of four buildings located on a 403-acre parcel bounded to the north by Morris Thomas Road, to the east by Midway Road, and to the west by Solway Road.
This site is a proposed 482-acre large scale data center being considered for Pine Island, MN. Currently (Oct 2025) it is facing major public opposition.
Tract is a data center park developer, who is seeking a second sight next to it's farmington campus in Dakota county, MN. Farmington Data campus to be mapped soon.

Meta, the parent company of Facebook, announced it will build an $800 million data center in Rosemount. Minnesota. The investment will see the 715,000-square-foot data center open on 280 acres east of Dakota County Technical College, on part of the University of Minnesota's UMore Park.

Meta Platforms Inc., through its subsidiary Jimnist LLC, has acquired over 200 acres of land in Rosemount located along County Road 42 and Blaine Avenue in February 2025. The $70 million purchase consisted of two parcels: one for $26.68 million and another for $43.32 million. While Meta currently has no specific development plans for the property, the company made the acquisition proactively to accommodate potential future business needs.

Meta intends to invest up to $837 million over several years to construct a data center in central Wisconsin. The company reportedly secured a unique agreement with the state in February, operating under an alias during the negotiation.

Microsoft has completed the purchase of an additional 1,030 acres of land for its Mount Pleasant data center campus in Racine County, Wisconsin. The 400 acres on Braun Road and Durand Avenue were purchased from the Village of Mount Pleasant for $63.2m, and 241 acres along County Highway H for $36.5m. The remaining 407 acres, also on Braun Road and Durand Avenue, were purchased from Creuziger Farms Inc. for $76m. Much of the land purchased was previously owned by Foxconn, which bought the parcel in 2017 intending to develop a manufacturing facility that would provide 10,000 jobs to the area. Foxconn ultimately only brought 1,454 jobs to the region.
properties.Status: Phase 2 paused, Phase 1 construction continuing on schedule

properties.Overview: Microsoft has acquired 240 additional acres in Wisconsin for data centers, near its Mount Pleasant project that was paused in early 2025. The company previously announced a $3.3 billion investment commitment in Wisconsin through 2026. In November 2024, plans were filed for a four-building data center campus on this land, though Microsoft hasn't confirmed specific details.

Digital Power Optimization (DPO), a US-based crypto and data center developer, will build a $200 million high-performance computing facility in Wisconsin Rapids, Wisconsin. DPO has secured land and power through a 50-year lease and partnership with Consolidated Water Power Company (CWPCo), a Billerud subsidiary, including interconnection rights to an existing substation and a firm power supply. The facility is expected to be operational in 2026.

A developer operating through Degas LLC is planning a major data center campus in Dodge County, Wisconsin. The proposed $567 million project would be located in Beaver Dam, approximately 60 miles northwest of Milwaukee. The development would occupy the 520-acre site formerly known as Beaver Dam Commerce Park, which is situated along US Highway 151, Hemlock Road, and County Highways A and W. The property is currently listed for sale at $20,000 per acre.

Red Wolf DCD Properties LLC has confirmed plans to build a 400 acre data center campus. The project aims to develop a six-building campus, totaling some 600MW across 1.8 million sq ft, as well as two on-site substations. - Data Center Dynamics

QTS, a Blackstone-owned firm, is expanding its data center footprint in the Kansas City area. The company has leased a substantial 756,000 square foot (70,234 sqm) facility, identified as Building B1, within the New Century Commerce Center (NCCC) in New Century, Kansas. This location in Johnson County places the future data center roughly 25 miles southwest of Kansas City. The newly constructed building, completed in 2023 by Van Trust Real Estate LLC, will be transformed into a state-of-the-art data center, although specific details regarding its specifications have not yet been disclosed. The NCCC itself is envisioned as a significant regional industrial park, benefiting from its strategic adjacency to the New Century Airfield, which provides valuable logistical benefits.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is planning a major data center campus in Tucson, Arizona, for a project codenamed "Project Blue." The development is a 290-acre site that will reportedly host at least three data centers, with some sources suggesting as many as 10 buildings are planned. These buildings could span a total of 2 million square feet. Construction on the first phase is scheduled to begin in 2026 and finish by 2029, with the first data centers potentially becoming operational in 2027.

properties.Overview: Carter Funds' critical infrastructure and data center division, Aphorio Carter Fund Management Company, LLC, expanded its portfolio in 2023 with the acquisition of the Tucson Tech Data Center. Located on an eight-acre site in Pima County, Arizona, the 133,450 sq ft (12,400 sqm) facility includes 40,790 sq ft (3,790 sqm) of raised floor space and is fully leased to TECfusions. Originally constructed in 1989, the building began its development into a data center in 2004.

properties.Overview: Ryan Companies plans to invest over $470 million to develop the Southwest Crossing Data Center, a 1.25 million square foot (116,130 square meter) campus. The real estate firm is working to rezone a planned warehouse site from General Industrial to General Industrial with a Planned Area Development Overlay to accommodate this data center project. On January 15, 2025, the Eloy Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval for this rezoning request. The development will include up to three buildings, each measuring 285,120 square feet (26,490 square meters), complemented by on-site substations.

Company Vermaland dubbed the La Osa Project, the potential facility would be located in Pinal County on a 3,300-acre site south of Eloy, which is a city in between Phoenix and Tucson. The land parcel is located along the Greene Canal. Vermaland filed a rezoning application for the site back in July, according to Data center Dynamics.

A 600-acre site in Pinal County, strategically located along I-10/Florence and dubbed the “Gateway into Casa Grande,” was acquired by Arizona Land Consulting. This property is poised for development into a mixed-use facility, with a portion dedicated to data center infrastructure alongside build-for-rent housing, light industrial, and commercial/retail components.

NTT Data has acquired 173 acres at the northeast intersection of Pecos and Crismon roads, east of Mesa, for $300 million. The company intends to develop a data center campus comprising seven buildings, with the first facility slated for operation by November 2028. The land was previously held by Levine Investments and Andrew Cohn through Mesa BA Land and Pacific Proving LLC. This group originally purchased 1,805 acres for $45 million in 2004. In September 2024, Levine, operating through Pacific Proving, received approval for the Pacific Proving Technology Campus. Plans for the Pacific Proving Technology campus include the construction of seven data halls offering nearly 1.7 million square feet (157,935 square meters) of total floor space, in addition to a 100,000-square-foot warehouse and a two-story office building.
This planned facility will be part of NTT's Pacific Proving Technology Park located in Mesa, Arizona.

Covering 160 acres, Novva’s first Arizona Data Center campus is located in Mesa, AZ. The campus includes five data halls, 1.3 million sq ft of data hall space, and 200,000 square feet of office space built over 2 phases. The Plan is also known as "Project Borealis". Novva predicts the project will take 10 million human hours to construct, and the first phase, will launch in late 2026. The data center provider will invest more than $3 billion to build the campus in two phases over the next decade.

Amazon.com Inc. is working on two separate data center projects in southeast Mesa, with each project containing two 227,000-square-foot data center buildings. The Pecos Campus, which spans 71.3 acres, is located at 10464 E. Pecos Road, just east of the Legacy Park sports complex. The other site is a 42.9-acre property located off Elliot Road, adjacent to Apple's existing data center in Mesa. Amazon acquired both properties in December 2021, paying $16.9 million for the Elliot Road land and over $18 million for the Pecos Road site.

Amazon Data Services has acquired land for a potential data center campus in Laveen, Phoenix. The 220-acre site, located near Loop 202 and Dobbins Road, was purchased for $277 million ($1.2 million per acre). The property, situated 20 minutes west of downtown Phoenix, lies within a planned industrial corridor intended for technology development. The area had previously attracted interest from TSMC as a possible location for their manufacturing facility.

Amazon is planning to build a data center campus on a 56-acre plot along highway 101, between Leavesly Road and Gilman Road in the City of Gilroy, California. The company paid $31.3 million for the plot in 2020 from local developers.The site would be developed in two phases. Phase I would include the first single-story data center building totaling approximately 218,000 square feet (20,250 sq m) and 25 diesel generators. Phase II, constructed within 4-7 years would consist of the second single-story data center building and as yet undetermined ‘alternative backup generation technologies’ to avoid the use of diesel-fired generators. The company said the facilities would have an average PUE of 1.18.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is securing over 400 acres in Arlington, Oregon, for a future data center campus, adding to their existing Oregon data centers in Morrow and Umatilla counties. The project involves purchasing 376 acres in 2024 ($10M) and an additional 30 acres in 2025 ($3M). Operation is years away due to permits, electricity, and tax break negotiations. Arlington and the port have been preparing the land for over a decade.

Google signed a 25-year government property lease excise tax, or GPLET, with the city of Mesa in July 2019 to assist in purchasing the more than 185 acres for the data center campus. The GPLET agreement put Google on the clock to complete the construction of the first phase of the data center by July 2025. Per a development agreement with Mesa, Google must also spend $600 million in capital expenditures. By 2027, Google must spend $800 million, with $240 million in taxable construction and have constructed at least 500,000 square feet of development. By 2029, those figures jump to a minimum spend of $1 billion, $300 million in taxable construction costs and at least 750,000 square feet of development built out.The entire project is expected to be finished in 2030. Google is also required to have an average annual salary for full-time data center employees of at least $65,000.

This facility will be a part of Google's Redhawk campus in Mesa, AZ. Phase II is expected to see Google build 280,000 square feet more. The plans also include facilities to house its electrical components and office space. The site takes up 185 acres near the northwest corner of Sossaman and Elliot roads. The facility will be powered by 400MW of power which will come from solar and wind farms in the state.

Microsoft acquired 300.7 acres from Mark IV Capital within the 4,300-acre Victory Logistics District, a master-planned industrial hub located in Fernley, Nevada. The site offers access to reliable power infrastructure, service from multiple fiber optic providers, and scalable land options.

Switch is planning second expansion of its data center campus in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Construction of a third data center building on the site is expected to begin "sooner rather than later," with the investment projected to be "several hundred million dollars."

Built in 2022, this data center was operated by Sentinum, Inc. ("Sentinum"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ault Alliance. Ault Alliance rebranded as Hyperscale Data, Inc. on September 10, 2024. Data center firm Hyperscale Data is aiming to expand the capacity of its southern Michigan facility to 300 megawatts. The existing facility occupies approximately 100,000 square feet within a larger 617,000 square foot building located on a 34.5-acre site. Benefiting from its proximity to power sources, the completion of the power upgrade is projected to take 44 months from the signing of a formal Letter of Authorization between Alliance Cloud and the utility, which is currently under negotiation.

Previously, Atlas Development LLC had proposed a $17 billion, 832-acre data center campus for the site, located near Newnan, Georgia. The original Project Sail was to include 13 data halls, each 378,000 square feet, totaling 4.9 million square feet, with a projected completion date of 2036. The site is located 45 miles south of Atlanta in Coweta County. Logistics real estate giant Prologis acquired Project Sail. The revised plan includes up to nine buildings with 4.34 million square feet of space.

Groot LLC has proposed "Project Pyramid," a five-building data center campus in West Memphis, Arkansas. Local media speculates that Google may be involved. Groot submitted plans for the project to the US Army Corps of Engineers for environmental approval. The data center campus will span 580 acres of a 1,178-acre property located on the south side of Bollinger Road. It will include five data center buildings and an on-site substation, with power supplied by Entergy Arkansas. Groot reportedly acquired the land parcels in November 2024.

Google has purchased 948.79 acres of rural land in Monroe County, Georgia, located along Rumble Road and I-75. The acquisition, finalized on September 26, 2025, for $42,636,285, is designated for a potential data center. Google stated that while there is no confirmed development timeline, the acquisition secures an option for future business growth. The site is situated near the Rumble Technology Campus, a development that received zoning approval for 12 data center buildings totaling 4.2 million sq ft. This parcel is part of a broader trend of data center development in Georgia, with a significant concentration around Atlanta. Monroe County is in the central part of the state, and Google already operates a data center campus in Douglas County near Atlanta.

In January 2024, OpenAI announced 'The Stargate Project,' a new venture planning to invest $500 billion in AI infrastructure over the next four years. The project's equity investors include SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and Abu Dhabi's MGX, with SoftBank managing financial responsibilities and OpenAI overseeing operations. In 2023, Lancium and former Bitcoin miner Crusoe began constructing a data center that is nearing completion and will be occupied by Oracle. It was later revealed that OpenAI would utilize the GPU capacity in Abilene for ChatGPT workloads. The Stargate Project has begun construction of data centers in Texas, with plans to expand to up to 20 facilities across different locations.
